NAHHAS:v4p303/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p303/r2.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p303/r2.claim: Teaching the Quran is an act of mercy that lets people recognize what pleases God and brings them near, and what displeases and distances them.
NAHHAS:v4p303/r2.anchor: أي من رحمته علم القرآن فبصر به رضاه الذي يقرب منه وسخطه الذي يباعد منه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p223#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p223#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p223#2/r4.claim: Teaching the Qur'an is a listed divine blessing; God taught it to people and gave special merit to its memorizers and understanders.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p223#2/r4.anchor: وقوله: علم القرآن تعديد نعمة أي هو من به وعلمه الناس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p223#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p223#2/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p223#2/r5.claim: The Prophet said the best people are those who learn and teach the Qur'an.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p223#2/r5.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «خيركم من تعلم القرآن وعلمه»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p223#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p223#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p223#2/r6.claim: He argues the Qur'an is uncreated: it is named fifty-four times in Scripture without being described or indicated as created, whereas human creation is explicit in eighteen places.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p223#2/r6.anchor: ومن الدليل على أن القرآن غير مخلوق: أن الله تعالى ذكر القرآن في كتابه في أربعة وخمسين موضعا

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p422#2/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p422#2/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p422#2/r3.claim: God taught the Qur'an to the Prophet so he could convey it to everyone, or made it easy for everyone to learn.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p422#2/r3.anchor: علمه النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم حتى أداه إلى جميع الناس . الثاني : سهل تعلمه على جميع الناس

TABRISI:55:1-13/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:55:1-13/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:55:1-13/r4.claim: Bayān can mean evidence leading to knowledge or the clarification of a meaning by distinguishing it from others.
TABRISI:55:1-13/r4.anchor: البيان هو الأدلة الموصلة إلى العلم

TABRISI:55:1-13/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:55:1-13/r11.speaker: الكلبي
TABRISI:55:1-13/r11.claim: Al-Kalbī says God taught Muhammad the Qurʾan and Muhammad taught it to his community.
TABRISI:55:1-13/r11.anchor: علم محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم القرآن وعلمه محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم أمته عن الكلبي

TABRISI:55:1-13/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:55:1-13/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:55:1-13/r12.claim: The teaching may answer Meccan claims that a human taught the Prophet: it was the Merciful who taught him, and the Qurʾan supplies needed religious wisdom.
TABRISI:55:1-13/r12.anchor: هو جواب لأهل مكة حين قالوا إنما يعلمه بشر

TABRISI:55:1-13/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:55:1-13/r13.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:55:1-13/r13.claim: Al-Zajjāj says “taught the Qurʾan” means God made it easy to remember.
TABRISI:55:1-13/r13.anchor: قال الزجاج: معنى { علم القرآن } يسره لأن يذكر

ELMALILI:55:1-13/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:55:1-13/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:55:1-13/r5.claim: Because teaching takes two objects, the first is omitted here; this presents teaching the Quran itself and leaves its recipients open to Gabriel, the Prophet, and the community.
ELMALILI:55:1-13/r5.anchor: bu mânaca burada birinci mef‘ul hazfedilmiş ve bu suretle maksad şuna veya buna ta‘lîmi değil

ELMALILI:55:1-13/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:55:1-13/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:55:1-13/r6.claim: Some read allama as making the Quran a sign or prophetic miracle, which needs no omitted object and parallels the preceding surah's opening miracle of the moon's splitting.
ELMALILI:55:1-13/r6.anchor: Bazıları da demişler ki burada عَلَّمَ alâmettendir; “Kur’ân’ı alâmet kıldı”

ELMALILI:55:1-13/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:55:1-13/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:55:1-13/r7.claim: Elmalılı favors translating the verb as ta‘lim etti, since that Turkish wording preserves both the teaching and sign interpretations.
ELMALILI:55:1-13/r7.anchor: tâlim etti” denilirse bu iki veche de işaret mahfuz kalmış olur

ELMALILI:55:1-13/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:55:1-13/r8.speaker: Âlûsî
ELMALILI:55:1-13/r8.claim: Even if a connection to signs is proposed, the verse must still be understood as teaching Quranic knowledge, including its words and meanings, with levels of insight extending to cosmic events.
ELMALILI:55:1-13/r8.anchor: Kāil bin münasebet de gösterse yine bunun ilim tâliminden olduğu bilinmek gerektir

ELMALILI:55:1-13/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:55:1-13/r9.speaker: İbn Mes‘ûd
ELMALILI:55:1-13/r9.claim: A report from Ibn Masud says the Quran contains knowledge concerning everything and explains everything, though human knowledge cannot encompass it all.
ELMALILI:55:1-13/r9.anchor: Kur’an’da her şeye dair ilim indirilmiş ve her şey beyan edilmiş ise de bizim ilmimiz onun hepsine yetişemez

ELMALILI:55:1-13/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:55:1-13/r10.speaker: İbn Abbas
ELMALILI:55:1-13/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas says that even if his camel's rope went missing, he would find it in God's Book.
ELMALILI:55:1-13/r10.anchor: İbn Abbas da demiştir ki: ‘Devemin bir ipi kaybolsa

ELMALILI:55:1-13/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:55:1-13/r11.speaker: Mürsî
ELMALILI:55:1-13/r11.claim: Mursi says the Quran gathers the sciences of earlier and later peoples, but its full reality is known only to God; interpretive knowledge passes from God to the Prophet, leading Companions, and their Successor heirs, except what God reserves.
ELMALILI:55:1-13/r11.anchor: Mürsî demiş[^7] ki: ‘Kur’an evvelîn ve âhirînin ulûmunu câmi‘dir.

ELMALILI:55:1-13/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:55:1-13/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:55:1-13/r12.claim: Some define teaching as awakening the mind to conceive meanings.
ELMALILI:55:1-13/r12.anchor: Bazıları ‘ta‘lîm’i; tasavvur-ı me‘ânî için nefsi tenbih diye târif etmişlerdir

ELMALILI:55:1-13/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:55:1-13/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:55:1-13/r13.claim: As the Hour approaches, teaching the Quran is presented as the greatest and most important blessing arising from divine mercy.
ELMALILI:55:1-13/r13.anchor: en büyük ve en mühim nimetin ta‘lîm-i Kur’an nimeti olduğu bu suretle anlatıldıktan sonra

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p106/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p106/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p106/r1.claim: God taught the Qur’an out of mercy; granting speech means humans can understand and teach one another, so they should use this exalted ability for instruction rather than punishment.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p106/r1.anchor: It is the merciful nature of the Almighty because of which He has taught them the Qur’ ān

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p109/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p109/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p109/r3.claim: The sūrah opens by presenting the Qur’an as divine mercy and teaching; human creation and speech make people fit to learn through revelation rather than punishment.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p109/r3.anchor: The sūrah begins with the declaration that the Qur’ ān is a manifestation of the graciousness of the Almighty.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p111/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p111/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p111/r1.claim: Revealing the Qur’an for instruction is a special mercy: it reforms mistaken beliefs and deeds so people can succeed in this life and the next, whereas they demand punishment.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p111/r1.anchor: He could have sent punishment as per their demand; however, out of His great mercy He blessed them with a benevolent scripture

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p53/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p53/r3.speaker: مقاتل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p53/r3.claim: He says the surah followed people's refusal to prostrate to الرحمن because they did not know the name, prompting الرحمن علم القرآن.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p53/r3.anchor: وسبب نزولها فيما قال مقاتل: أنه لما نزل وإذا قيل لهم اسجدوا للرحمن الآية،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p53/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p53/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p53/r4.claim: Another occasion was the claim that a human taught the Prophet; God answered that the Merciful taught the Qur'an.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p53/r4.anchor: وقيل: لما قالوا إنما يعلمه بشر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p54/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p54/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p54/r1.claim: Teaching the Qur'an is an effect of mercy and heals hearts; الرحمن is apparently the subject and علم القرآن its predicate, though another parse supplies an omitted predicate.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p54/r1.anchor: الرحمن، علم القرآن، فذكر ما نشأ عن صفة الرحمة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p54/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p54/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p54/r2.claim: Teaching the Qur'an comes first as the highest blessing, foundation of religion and salvation for whoever holds it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p54/r2.anchor: ولما عدد نعمه تعالى، بدأ من نعمه بما هو أعلى رتبها، وهو تعليم القرآن،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p54/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p54/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p54/r3.claim: Humans are named after teaching because they are the intended learners; creation follows as the means to religious and Qur'anic instruction.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p54/r3.anchor: ولما ذكر تعليم القرآن ولم يذكر المعلم، ذكره بعد في قوله: خلق الإنسان،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p54/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p54/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p54/r5.claim: علّم takes two objects and omits the first, possibly Gabriel, Muhammad, or the learner. Fakhr al-Din al-Razi instead says the second is omitted; Abu Hayyan identifies the missing object as first.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p54/r5.anchor: وعلم متعدية إلى اثنين، حذف أولهما لدلالة المعنى عليه، وهو جبريل،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p54/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p54/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p54/r6.claim: He calls it remote to interpret 'taught the Qur'an' as making it a sign; the clauses instead independently enumerate blessings.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p54/r6.anchor: وأبعد من ذهب إلى أن معنى علم القرآن: جعله علامة وآية

BIQAI-FULL:v7p371/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p371/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p371/r1.claim: After the preceding surah’s emphasis on sovereignty and power, this surah counts blessings in both worlds; universal mercy completes kingship, and its opening name signals that theme.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p371/r1.anchor: قصر هذه السورة على تعداد نعمه على خلقه في الدارين

BIQAI-FULL:v7p371/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p371/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p371/r2.claim: Teaching the Qur’an is the greatest blessing: it is written and recited, gathers good, and distinguishes confusion; making this divine attribute accessible shows God can teach whom He wills.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p371/r2.anchor: المرئي المشهود بالكتابة والمتلو المسموع الجامع لكل خير

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:1/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:1/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:1/r1.claim: The surah opens with al-Rahman to express God's immense mercy and blessings for all servants, while religion is the greatest gift to rational beings and the Qur'an its highest gift to humanity.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:1/r1.anchor: Sûreye Cenâb-ı Allah’ın rahmetinin enginliğini, kulluk görevini yapsın yapmasın bütün kullarına nimet vermesini ifade eden Rahmân ismiyle ve O’nun Kur’an’ı öğretmesiyle başlanmakta

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:1/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:1/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:1/r2.claim: Some exegetes take the verb usually meaning “taught” as “made a sign”: God made the Qur'an a miracle proving Muhammad's prophethood and containing signs for reflective readers.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:55:1/r2.anchor: “Öğretti” anlamına gelen fiile “alâmet kıldı” mânası da verilebildiğinden bazı müfessirler bu âyetler için şöyle bir yorum yapmışlardır

QIRAAT-ER:55:2:2#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:55:2:2#1/r1.speaker: Ibn Kathīr and others
QIRAAT-ER:55:2:2#1/r1.claim: Ibn Kathīr and others omit hamza in Qurān; the reading leaves meaning unchanged, smooths pronunciation, and reflects a Hijazi tendency to soften hamza.
QIRAAT-ER:55:2:2#1/r1.anchor: Hamza dropped: Qurʾān → Qurān. Ibn Kathīr and others read without hamza

BURSEVI:v9p235#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p235#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p235#2/r9.claim: God taught Muhammad the Quran through Gabriel, and Muhammad in turn teaches the community.
BURSEVI:v9p235#2/r9.anchor: بواسطة جبريل عليه السلام وبواسطة محمد عليه السلام غيره من الأمة

BURSEVI:v9p235#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p235#2/r10.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v9p235#2/r10.claim: Al-Kāshifī paraphrases the teaching as making learning easy for Muhammad and enabling him to teach others.
BURSEVI:v9p235#2/r10.anchor: يعني آسان كردانيده مراورا آموختن وديكر انرا آموزانيدن

BURSEVI:v9p235#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p235#2/r11.speaker: ابن عطاء
BURSEVI:v9p235#2/r11.claim: As God taught Adam the names and distinguished him by them, He specially distinguished Muhammad's community by teaching it the Quran and elevating it above other nations; He taught it in pre-eternity and manifested the teaching at creation.
BURSEVI:v9p235#2/r11.anchor: أراد أن يخص أمة محمد بخاصة مثله

BURSEVI:v9p235#2/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p235#2/r12.speaker: ابن عطاء
BURSEVI:v9p235#2/r12.claim: Although Gabriel mediates Quran teaching outwardly, it is direct without mediation in the inward, special sense.
BURSEVI:v9p235#2/r12.anchor: من الوجه العام لكنه كان بلا واسطة في المعنى من الوجه الخاص

BURSEVI:v9p235#2/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p235#2/r13.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v9p235#2/r13.claim: God granted complete readiness to receptive people in pre-eternity; Quran names speech in its unified origin, whereas Furqan names its differentiated end, so Quran teaching does not depend on human creation, but expressive speech does.
BURSEVI:v9p235#2/r13.anchor: الكلام الإلهي قرآن باعتبار الجمع والبداية وفرقان باعتبار الفرق والنهاية

BURSEVI:v9p235#2/r14.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p235#2/r14.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p235#2/r14.claim: The order follows this distinction: Quran teaching precedes human creation, while creating the human precedes teaching expression.
BURSEVI:v9p235#2/r14.anchor: ولذا قدم تعليم القرآن على خلق الإنسان وخلقه على تعليم البيان

BURSEVI:v9p235#2/r15.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p235#2/r15.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p235#2/r15.claim: Teaching and making learning easy come from God, not independently from teachers or memorizers; scripture likewise attributes Adam's names, David's armor-making, Jesus's learning, and the hidden knowledge given to al-Khiḍr to God.
BURSEVI:v9p235#2/r15.anchor: وفي الآية إشارة إلى أن التعليم والتسهيل إنما هو من الله تعالى لا من المعلمين والحافظين

QASHANI:55:1-2/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:55:1-2/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:55:1-2/r2.claim: The Qur’an is the perfect human preparedness called the Qur’anic intellect, gathering all realities, qualities, and rulings in human nature; it becomes differentiated as Furqan at the end through mercy of the All-Compassionate.
QASHANI:55:1-2/r2.anchor: الاستعداد الكامل الإنساني المسمى بالعقل القرآني الجامع للأشياء كلها

ALUSI-FULL:v27p98/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p98/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p98/r1.claim: The Qur’an is the greatest blessing: it underpins religious and worldly happiness, measures the heavenly scriptures, and guides the highest aspirations.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p98/r1.anchor: لأنه أعظم النعم شاناوأرفعها مكانا كيف لا وهو مداره للسعادة الدينية والدنيوية وعيار على الكتب السماوية

ALUSI-FULL:v27p98/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p98/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p98/r2.claim: Qur’an is the second object of ʿallama; the first, understood as humanity, is omitted, and the construction reflects teaching as a general blessing.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p98/r2.anchor: ونصبه على أنه مفعول ثان لعلم ومفعوله الأول محذوف لدلالة المعنى عليه أي علم الإنسان القرآن

ALUSI-FULL:v27p98/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p98/r3.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v27p98/r3.claim: The Imam treats the omitted object as the second object, leaving the first unexpressed to show that the blessing lies in teaching generally.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p98/r3.anchor: وسها الإمام فحسب أن المحذوف المفعول الثاني حيث قال : علم لا بد له من مفعول ثان

ALUSI-FULL:v27p98/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p98/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p98/r4.claim: Al-Alusi allows that the Imam may mean another object is needed alongside Qur’an, so the Imam’s error is not certain.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p98/r4.anchor: ويمكن أن يقال : أراد أنه لا بد له من مفعول آخر مع هذاالمفعول فلا جزم بسهوه

ALUSI-FULL:v27p98/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p98/r5.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v27p98/r5.claim: One proposed omitted learner is Gabriel or the nearest angels; this implies Qur’an is God’s speech.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p98/r5.anchor: وقيل : المقدر جبريل عليه السلام أو الملائكة المقربين عليهم السلام وقيل : محمد

ALUSI-FULL:v27p98/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p98/r6.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v27p98/r6.claim: Another proposed omitted learner is Muhammad; this likewise implies Qur’an is God’s speech.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p98/r6.anchor: وقيل : محمد صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم وعلى القولين يتضمن ذلك الإشارة إلى أن القرآن كلام الله عز وجل

ALUSI-FULL:v27p98/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p98/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p98/r7.claim: The human learner is the clearest and most contextually fitting estimate for the omitted object.

ALUSI-FULL:v27p98/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p98/r8.speaker: ابن الصلاح
ALUSI-FULL:v27p98/r8.claim: Ibn al-Salah says Qur’an recitation is a grace given to humans, not angels, who eagerly listen to humans reciting it.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p98/r8.anchor: نقلاعنابن الصلاح من أن قراءة القرآن كرامة أكرم الله تعالى بها البشر فقد ورد أن الملائكة لم يعطوا ذلك وأنهم حريصون لذلك على استماعه من الإنس

ALUSI-FULL:v27p98/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p98/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p98/r9.claim: Al-Alusi hesitates to generalize that angels cannot recite Qur’an because texts state that Gabriel recited it, though he doubts the report may be accepted even with Gabriel excepted.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p98/r9.anchor: وإنما لم أعتبر عمومه للنصوص الدالة على أن جبريل عليه السلام كان يقرأالقرآن

ALUSI-FULL:v27p98/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p98/r10.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v27p98/r10.claim: An alternative derives ʿallama from ʿalāma: God made Qur’an a sign for reflection, prophethood, and a miracle, paralleling the prior surah’s opening miracle.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p98/r10.anchor: وقيل : ( علم ) من العلامة ولا تقدير أي جعل القرآن علامة وآية لمن اعتبر أو علامة للنبوة ومعجزة

ALUSI-FULL:v27p98#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p98#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p98#2/r1.claim: Al-Alusi calls the ‘made a sign’ derivation far-fetched, even if its advocate offers many parallels; the word should be understood as teaching.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p98#2/r1.anchor: وقد أبعد القائل ولوأبدى ألف مناسبة فالذي ينبغي أن يعلم أنه من التعليم

ALUSI-FULL:v27p98#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p98#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p98#2/r2.claim: Teaching Qur’an imparts both its wording and reliable understanding of its meanings, whose allusions can reach knowledge of cosmic events; God has omitted nothing from it.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p98#2/r2.anchor: بل بمعنى إفادة ذلك والعلم بمعانيه على وجه يعتد به وهو متفاوت وقد يصل إلى العلم بالحوادث الكونية من إشاراته ورموزه

ALUSI-FULL:v27p98#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p98#2/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
ALUSI-FULL:v27p98#2/r3.claim: A report raised to the Prophet says that if God had omitted anything from Qur’an, He would have omitted even an atom, mustard seed, or mosquito.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p98#2/r3.anchor: أخرج أبو الشيخ في كتاب العظمة عن أبي هريرة مرفوعاإن الله لو أغفل شيئالأغفل الذرة والخردلة والبعوضة

ALUSI-FULL:v27p98#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p98#2/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v27p98#2/r4.claim: Ibn Masud says Qur’an contains knowledge of everything and clarifies everything, though people fall short of grasping what it clarifies.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p98#2/r4.anchor: أخرج ابن جرير وابن أبي حاتم عن ابن مسعود أنزل في هذا القرآن علم كل شيء وبين لنا فيه كل شيء ولكن علمنا يقصر

ALUSI-FULL:v27p98#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p98#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v27p98#2/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says that if he lost a camel’s halter, he would find it in God’s Book.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p98#2/r5.anchor: وقال ابن عباس : لو ضاع لي عقال بعير لوجدته في كتاب الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v27p98#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p98#2/r6.speaker: المرسي
ALUSI-FULL:v27p98#2/r6.claim: Al-Mursi says Qur’an gathers the knowledge of the first and last, truly encompassed only by its Speaker; the Prophet, leading Companions, and Successors inherited most of it, before later scholars weakened.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p98#2/r6.anchor: وقال المرسي : جمع القرآن علوم الأولين والآخرين بحيث لم يحط بها علما حقيقة إلا المتكلم به

ALUSI-FULL:v27p98#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p98#2/r7.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v27p98#2/r7.claim: Some define teaching as preparing the self to conceive meanings.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p98#2/r7.anchor: وفسر بعضهم التعليم بتبنيه النفس لتصور المعاني

ALUSI-FULL:v27p98#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p98#2/r8.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v27p98#2/r8.claim: The Imam permits a figurative sense: making a person able to know Qur’an, as in God’s making it easy to remember.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p98#2/r8.anchor: وجوز الإمام أن يراد به هنا جعل الشخص بحيث يعلم القرآن كقوله تعالى : ( ولقديسرنا القرآن للذكر )

ALUSI-FULL:v27p127#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p127#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p127#2/r2.claim: The unfolding of spiritual knowledge is likened to following a recitation whose explanation God undertakes.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p127#2/r2.anchor: فإذا قرأناهفاتبع قرآنه ثم إن علينا بيانه

QUSHAYRI:v3p262/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p262/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p262/r2.claim: The Merciful whom monotheists acknowledge and disbelievers reject is the one who taught the Quran.
QUSHAYRI:v3p262/r2.anchor: الرحمن الذي عرفه الموحدون وجحده الكافرون هو الذي علم القرآن

QUSHAYRI:v3p262/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p262/r3.speaker: قيل
QUSHAYRI:v3p262/r3.claim: The Merciful taught them by showing mercy, protecting them from idolatry, honoring them with faith, and binding them to the word of piety.
QUSHAYRI:v3p262/r3.anchor: ويقال : الرحمن الذي رحمهم ، وعن الشرك عصمهم

QUSHAYRI:v3p262/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p262/r4.speaker: قيل
QUSHAYRI:v3p262/r4.claim: Another formulation says the Real alone acquainted His servants with the Quran.
QUSHAYRI:v3p262/r4.anchor: ويقال : انفرد الحق عرفهم بالقرآن لعباده

QUSHAYRI:v3p262/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p262/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p262/r5.claim: God's customary generosity shares with the community what He grants the Prophet in a manner suited to them: after teaching Muhammad what he did not know, He declared that the Merciful taught the Quran.
QUSHAYRI:v3p262/r5.anchor: أجرى الله سنته أنه إذا أعطى نبينا شيئا أشرك أمته فيه على ما يليق بصفاتهم

QUSHAYRI:v3p262/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p262/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p262/r6.claim: As God taught Adam the names and commanded him to present them to the angels, He taught Muhammad the Quran, which the Prophet taught the Muslims; prayer requires the Fatiha and makes the worshipper commune with his Lord.
QUSHAYRI:v3p262/r6.anchor: علم الله آدم الأسماء كلها ثم أمره بعرضها على الملائكة

QUSHAYRI:v3p262/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p262/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p262/r7.claim: God asks Adam to report what He taught him to the angels, while asking the worshipper to address Him with what He taught; He treats the servants' children with a tenderness their fathers do not receive.
QUSHAYRI:v3p262/r7.anchor: قال لآدم : أذكر ما علمتك للملائكة . وقال لنا : ناجني يا عبدي بما علمتك

QUSHAYRI:v3p262/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p262/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p262/r8.claim: As He taught Adam the names of created things and told him to inform the angels, God taught people His speech and names and invited them to recite and converse with Him.
QUSHAYRI:v3p262/r8.anchor: وعلمنا كلامه وأسماءه فقال : اقرأوا علي وخاطبوا به معي

QUSHAYRI:v3p262/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p262/r9.speaker: قيل
QUSHAYRI:v3p262/r9.claim: The spirits were taught the Quran directly before embodiment; children then learn it before their spirits have known or heard anyone, and the poem portrays love as arriving before the lover knew love.
QUSHAYRI:v3p262/r9.anchor: ويقال : علم الأرواح القرآن - قبل تركيبها في الأجساد بلا واسطة

QUSHAYRI:v3p262/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p262/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p262/r10.claim: The poet's lines recall past days when God was teaching them the Quran, expressing their longing for that divine instruction.
QUSHAYRI:v3p262/r10.anchor: ويقال : سقيا لأيام مضت - وهو يعلمنا القرآن

QUSHAYRI:v3p262/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p262/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p262/r11.claim: God's mercy is what brings people to the Quran; recitation of the Quran is not what brings them to His mercy.
QUSHAYRI:v3p262/r11.anchor: ويقال : برحمته علمهم القرآن ؛ فبرحمته وصلوا إلى القرآن

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p438#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p438#2/r3.speaker: الكلبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p438#2/r3.claim: Al-Kalbī says God taught the Qurʾān to Muḥammad.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p438#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p438#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p438#2/r4.claim: An alternative interpretation says God made the Qurʾān easy to remember.

BAYDAWI-FULL:55:1-4/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:1-4/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:1-4/r3.claim: The Qurʾān is presented first as the greatest religious blessing: it grounds religion and law, is the most precious book, and by its inimitability and comprehensive content validates its message.
BAYDAWI-FULL:55:1-4/r3.anchor: إنعامه بالقرآن وتنزيله وتعليمه، فإنه أساس الدين

SULAMI:v2p292#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p292#2/r1.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p292#2/r1.claim: They compare God's teaching all names to angels with His teaching Muhammad the Qur'an, which He presents to Himself; the disputing high assembly means the angels.
SULAMI:v2p292#2/r1.anchor: قال بعضهم : علم الأسماء كلها ثم عرضهم على الملائكة وعلم محمدا القرآن وعرضه على نفسه فقال : فيما يختصم الملأ الأعلى يعني الملائكة

SULAMI:v2p292#2/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p292#2/r2.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p292#2/r2.claim: They say God taught the spirit the Qur'an before the body, so bodies received and learned it by following the spirits.
SULAMI:v2p292#2/r2.anchor: وقال بعضهم : علم الروح القرآن قبل الجسد ، فالأجساد أخذت القرآن وتعلمته تبعا للأرواح

SULAMI:v2p292#2/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p292#2/r3.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p292#2/r3.claim: Wāsiṭī traces the chosen community's inheritance of scripture and human dignity to God's own teaching, citing 35:32 and 17:70.
SULAMI:v2p292#2/r3.anchor: قال الواسطي رحمة الله عليه : اورثهم تعليم الحق إياهم الاصطفائية وهو انه لما كان الحق معهم اجيز عنهم فقال : ﴿ أورثنا الكتاب الذين اصطفينا من عبادنا ﴾

SULAMI:v2p292#2/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p292#2/r4.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p292#2/r4.claim: Wāsiṭī says the past-tense wording that the All-Merciful taught the Qur'an expresses divine care and invitation.
SULAMI:v2p292#2/r4.anchor: وقال أيضا : ﴿ الرحمن علم القرآن ﴾ ذكر بلفظ الماضي عناية ودعاية

SULAMI:v2p292#2/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p292#2/r5.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p292#2/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAṭā likens teaching Muhammad's community the Qur'an to teaching Adam the names: God favored the community over other peoples, with teaching known eternally and its effects manifested at creation.
SULAMI:v2p292#2/r5.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : لما قال الله تعالى : ﴿ وعلم آدم الأسماء كلها ﴾ أراد أن يخص أمة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

SULAMI:v2p292#2/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p292#2/r6.speaker: الحسين
SULAMI:v2p292#2/r6.claim: Al-Ḥusayn says the All-Merciful taught the spirits the Qur'an directly, and souls then learned it through intermediaries.
SULAMI:v2p292#2/r6.anchor: قال الحسين : الرحمن علم الأرواح القرآن شفاها ومخاطبة فأخذته الأنفس وتعلمته بتلقين الوسائط

SULAMI:v2p292#2/r7.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p292#2/r7.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p292#2/r7.claim: They take the teaching of the Qur'an as an explanation of God's teaching Muhammad what he had not known.
SULAMI:v2p292#2/r7.anchor: وقال بعضهم في قوله : ﴿ الرحمن علم القرآن ﴾ هو تفسير قوله : ﴿ وعلمك ما لم تكن تعلم ﴾

BIQAI-FULL:v7p372/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p372/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p372/r1.claim: The Qur'an is the greatest blessing, the summit and foundation of the heavenly books, clarifying what pleases God and what must be avoided; it leads to the promised abode.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p372/r1.anchor: أجل النعم نعمة ادين التي تتبعها نعمة الدنيا والآخرة

BIQAI-FULL:v7p372/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p372/r2.speaker: جعفر بن الزبير
BIQAI-FULL:v7p372/r2.claim: Jaʿfar says the whole Qur'an is miraculous and its arrangement overpowers opponents, while some passages disclose its eloquence more immediately; he points to Sūrat al-Qamar's concise stories that still complete their aims and admonitions.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p372/r2.anchor: وقال الإمام جعفر بن الزبير : من المعلوم أن الكتاب العزيز وإن كانت آية كلها معجزة باهرة وسورة في جليل النظم وبديع التأليف قاطعة بالخصوم قاهرة

BIQAI-FULL:v7p372/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p372/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p372/r3.claim: The commentary gives the address to earth and sky and the command to proclaim as examples of instantly evident Qur'anic eloquence.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p372/r3.anchor: { وقيل يا أرض ابتلغي ماءك ويا سماء أقلعي } [ هود : 44 ]

BIQAI-FULL:v7p372/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p372/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p372/r5.claim: Sūrat al-Raḥmān follows al-Qamar to address both humans and jinn, establish proof for both kinds, and repeatedly remind them of God's favors.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p372/r5.anchor: فاتبعت سورة القمر بسورة الرحمن تنبيها للثقلين وإعذارا إليهم وتقريرا للجنسين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p106/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p106/r1.speaker: ابن السائب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p106/r1.claim: Ibn al-Saib says God taught the Quran to Muhammad, and Muhammad taught it to his community.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p106/r1.anchor: أحدهما علمه محمدا وعلم محمد أمته قاله ابن السائب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p106/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p106/r2.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p106/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj interprets the phrase as God making the Quran easy.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p489#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p489#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p489#2/r1.claim: God's favor and mercy include sending the Quran to His servants and making its memorization and understanding easy for those He shows mercy.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p489#2/r1.anchor: يخبر تعالى عن فضله ورحمته بخلقه: أنه أنزل على عباده القرآن ويسر حفظه وفهمه على من رحمه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r1.claim: Zamakhsharī places the Quran first among divine favors because religion is the foremost favor; its revelation and teaching are the highest-ranked revelation and the summit, proof, and standard of heavenly books.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r1.anchor: وهي نعمة الدين ، فقدم من نعمة الدين ما هو في أعلى مراتبها وأقصى مراقيها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r2.claim: Mentioning human creation after the Quran shows that humanity was created for religion and to know revelation and scripture; the purpose of human creation is presented as prior to creation.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r2.anchor: وأخر ذكر خلق الإنسان عن ذكره ، ثم أتبعه إياه : ليعلم أنه إنما خلقه للدين

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r4.claim: Al-Raḥmān is the subject; the following verbs with their pronouns form successive predicates without conjunctions, matching a listing of favors and making each clause an independent rebuke to deniers.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r4.anchor: أخبار مترادفة ، وإخلاؤها من العاطف لمجيئها على نمط التعديد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r5.claim: He illustrates the rebuke by listing how Zayd was helped after poverty, lowliness, and scarcity, then asking what kindness he could deny.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r5.anchor: زيد أغناك بعد فقر ، أعزك بعد ذل ، كثرك بعد قلة ، فعل بك ما لم يفعل أحد بأحد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r10.claim: The first clauses omit conjunctions so each independently rebukes deniers by enumerating benefactions; conjunctions resume for clauses that suit and approach each other.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r10.anchor: ثم رد الكلام إلى منهاجه بعد التبكيت في وصل ما يجب وصله للتناسب والتقارب بالعاطف

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r12.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p442/r12.claim: An alternative explanation says that teaching the Quran made it a sign and a miracle.

MUQATIL:55:1-4/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:55:1-4/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:55:1-4/r2.claim: The al-Rahman whom they denied taught the Qur'an, created Adam, and taught him speech—the explanation of all things.
MUQATIL:55:1-4/r2.anchor: فقال: { الرحمن } الذي أنكروه هو الذي { علم القرآن خلق الإنسان } [آية: 3] يعني آدم

NASAFI-FULL:v4p199#7/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p199#7/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p199#7/r1.claim: The word al-insan in the creation verse may mean humanity as a kind, Adam, or Muhammad.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p199#7/r1.anchor: ﴿ الرحمن علم القرآن خلق الإنسان ﴾ اى الجنس أو آدم أو محمدا عليهما السلام

QURTUBI-FULL:55:1-5/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:1-5/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:55:1-5/r2.claim: God taught the Qurʾan to His Prophet, who then conveyed it to all people.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:1-5/r2.anchor: أي علمه نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم حتى أداه إلى جميع الناس

QURTUBI-FULL:55:1-5/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:1-5/r5.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:55:1-5/r5.claim: Al-Zajjāj explains teaching the Qurʾan as making it easy to remember and recite, supported by 54:17.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:1-5/r5.anchor:
وقال الزجاج: معنى «علم القرآن» أي سهله لأن يذكر ويقرأ كما قال:
ولقد يسرنا القرآن للذكر

QURTUBI-FULL:55:1-5/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:55:1-5/r6.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:55:1-5/r6.claim: Another explanation is that the Qurʾan was made a sign for what people worship.
QURTUBI-FULL:55:1-5/r6.anchor: وقيل: جعله علامة لما تعبد الناس به

RAZI-FULL:v29p75#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p75#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p75#2/r1.claim: If Qur’an teaching means teaching angels, God taught them before creating humans; the preserved Qur’an is touched only by the purified and then sent down from the Lord of the worlds.
RAZI-FULL:v29p75#2/r1.anchor: فعلم تعالى ملائكته المقربين القرآن حقيقة

RAZI-FULL:v29p75#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p75#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p75#2/r2.claim: This order pairs celestial matters with earthly ones and names the celestial first: Qur’an teaching above is paired with teaching expression to humans below.
RAZI-FULL:v29p75#2/r2.anchor: ذكر أمورا علوية وأمورا سفلية ، وكل علوي قابله بسفلي ، وقدم العلويات على السفليات

RAZI-FULL:v29p75#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p75#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p75#2/r5.claim: Alternatively, Qur’an teaching comes first because it is the greatest favor; ‘created humanity, taught him expression’ then explains how that teaching is given.
RAZI-FULL:v29p75#2/r5.anchor: تقديم تعليم القرآن إشارة إلى كونه أتم نعمة وأعظم إنعاما

STUDYQURAN:55:2/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:2/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:55:2/r1.claim: The verb's placement after al-Raḥmān makes teaching revelation intrinsic to God's compassion; revelation is a blessing sustaining creation.
STUDYQURAN:55:2/r1.anchor: That the verb taught comes directly after the Divine Name al-Raḥmān indicates that teaching revelation is intrinsic to God’s compassionate nature.

STUDYQURAN:55:2/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:2/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:55:2/r2.claim: Teaching is an essential divine function toward humanity: God teaches Adam and all humans, created for knowledge, before giving commands, laws, and judgment.
STUDYQURAN:55:2/r2.anchor: human beings are created for knowledge and God teaches Adam and thus all of humanity (2:31) before commanding, providing laws, and judging.

STUDYQURAN:55:2/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:2/r3.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:55:2/r3.claim: Some commentators read the verse as an answer to disbelievers who claimed a human taught the Prophet and the Quran.
STUDYQURAN:55:2/r3.anchor: According to some commentators, this verse is a direct response to the disbelievers who said

STUDYQURAN:55:2/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:2/r4.speaker: Others
STUDYQURAN:55:2/r4.claim: Others see an allusion to God's making the Quran easy to learn, echoed by the preceding sūrah's refrain.
STUDYQURAN:55:2/r4.anchor: Others understand it as an allusion to the manner in which God has made the Quran easy to learn

STUDYQURAN:55:2/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:55:2/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:55:2/r5.claim: The verse may instead begin a new thought: God taught the Quran.
STUDYQURAN:55:2/r5.anchor: This verse could also be understood as the beginning of a new thought

TAB-FULL:v22p168#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p168#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v22p168#2/r1.claim: God’s teaching enables people to follow His commands, avoid what angers Him, gain abundant reward, and escape painful punishment.
TAB-FULL:v22p168#2/r1.anchor: وعملكم بما أمركم به، وبتجنبكم ما يسخطه عليكم، فتستوجبوا بذلك جزيل ثوابه، وتنجوا من أليم عقابه

TAB-FULL:v22p168#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p168#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v22p168#2/r2.claim: Qatada calls God’s teaching of the Qur’an a tremendous blessing.
TAB-FULL:v22p168#2/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، أنه قال في تفسير {الرحمن علم القرآن} [الرحمن: 2] قال: «نعمة والله عظيمة»

SAMIN-DURR:55:2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:55:2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:55:2/r1.claim: The stronger analysis derives علم from teaching and treats it as a transitive verb taking two objects, with the first object omitted.
SAMIN-DURR:55:2/r1.anchor: فيه وجهان، أظهرهما: أنها علم المتعدية إلى اثنين أي: عرف، من التعليم، فعلى هذا المفعول الأول محذوف

SAMIN-DURR:55:2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:55:2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:55:2/r2.claim: One proposed omitted first object is Gabriel: God taught Gabriel the Quran.
SAMIN-DURR:55:2/r2.anchor: فعلى هذا المفعول الأول محذوف فقيل: تقديره: علم جبريل القرآن.

SAMIN-DURR:55:2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:55:2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:55:2/r3.claim: Another proposed omitted first object is Muhammad: God taught Muhammad the Quran.
SAMIN-DURR:55:2/r3.anchor: وقيل: علم محمدا. وقيل: علم الإنسان.

SAMIN-DURR:55:2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:55:2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:55:2/r4.claim: The author prefers humanity as the omitted first object because the meaning is general and the next verse, “created man,” supports it.
SAMIN-DURR:55:2/r4.anchor: وقيل: علم الإنسان. وهذا أولى لعمومه، ولأن قوله " خلق الإنسان " دال عليه.

SAMIN-DURR:55:2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:55:2/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:55:2/r5.claim: An alternative derives علم from “sign”: God made the Quran a sign and a verse to which people should attend.
SAMIN-DURR:55:2/r5.anchor: والثاني: أنها من العلامة. فالمعنى: جعله علامة وآية يعتنى بها.

SAMIN-DURR:55:2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:55:2/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:55:2/r6.claim: The successive clauses omit conjunctions because they enumerate blessings in a tightly connected list; they appear to be predicates.
SAMIN-DURR:55:2/r6.anchor: وهذه الجمل التي جيء بها من غير عاطف لأنها سيقت لتعديد نعمة كقولك:

SAMIN-DURR:55:2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:55:2/r7.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:55:2/r7.claim: Abu al-Baqa treats “created man” as a new independent clause and allows “taught him” to be a prospective circumstantial clause with an implied قد.
SAMIN-DURR:55:2/r7.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء: و " خلق الإنسان " مستأنف وكذلك " علمه " يجوز أن يكون حالا من الإنسان مقدرة

SAMIN-DURR:55:2/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:55:2/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:55:2/r8.claim: The author says Abu al-Baqa's parsing is not apparent; the preceding analysis is the apparent one, also the only one al-Zamakhshari mentions.
SAMIN-DURR:55:2/r8.anchor: وهذا ليس بظاهر بل الظاهر ما قدمته ولم يذكر الزمخشري غيره.

SAMIN-DURR:55:2/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:55:2/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:55:2/r9.claim: Although creation precedes teaching in time, teaching the Quran is placed first because it is the cause of the human being's creation.
SAMIN-DURR:55:2/r9.anchor: قيل: لأن التعليم هو السبب في إيجاده وخلقه.

ZAJJAJ:v5p95/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p95/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p95/r2.claim: Teaching the Qurʾān means making it easy for it to be recited or remembered.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p133#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p133#2/r1.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p133#2/r1.claim: When 17:110 was revealed, Meccan disbelievers said they knew only Musaylima, the Rahman of al-Yamama; 25:60 records their denial of the name.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p133#2/r1.anchor: قال كفار مكة: ما نعرف إلا مسيلمة، رحمان اليمامة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p133#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p133#2/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p133#2/r2.claim: God identifies himself by mentioning his works so that people will recognize him and affirm his oneness.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p133#2/r2.anchor: فأخبر الله عن نفسه، وذكر صنعه ليعرف فيوحد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p133#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p133#2/r3.speaker: صاحب النظم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p133#2/r3.claim: Although “taught” normally takes two objects, only one is stated; the recipient is understood, as in saying that Zayd fed food.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p133#2/r3.anchor: قوله (علم) يقتضي مفعولين ولم يجيء هاهنا إلا واحد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p133#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p133#2/r4.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p133#2/r4.claim: God taught the Qur’an to Muhammad, who in turn taught it to his community.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p133#2/r4.anchor: علم القرآن محمدا وعلمه محمد -صلى الله عليه وسلم- أمته

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p133#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p133#2/r5.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p133#2/r5.claim: He explains teaching the Qur’an as making it easy to remember or recite.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:55:1-5/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:55:1-5/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:55:1-5/r1.claim: God taught the Qur’an to His Prophet, contrary to the polytheists’ claim that a human taught it to him.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:55:1-5/r1.anchor: علم نبيه عليه السلام القرآن، ليس كما يقول المشركون

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:55:1-5/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:55:1-5/r2.speaker: قيل
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:55:1-5/r2.claim: An alternative says God made the Qur’an easy to remember and taught it to this community until they memorized it.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:55:1-5/r2.anchor: وقيل: معناه: يسر القرآن لأن يذكر، فعلمه هذه الأمة حتى حفظوه.

BURSEVI:v9p236/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p236/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p236/r1.claim: God taught the Prophet the Quran and divine mysteries, as expressed in the statement that He taught him what he did not know.
BURSEVI:v9p236/r1.anchor: وعلمك ما لم تكن تعلم وعلم الإنسان البيان

BURSEVI:v9p236#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p236#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p236#2/r1.claim: Bursevi argues that divine speech can be expressed in every language; although inner speech is bare of linguistic coverings, its descents and communications take on a language as a garment.
BURSEVI:v9p236#2/r1.anchor: والكلام النفسي عار عن جميع الأكسية قلت : نعم ولكنه في مراتب التنزلات والاسترسالات لا بد له من الكسوة

BURSEVI:v9p236#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p236#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p236#2/r2.claim: From personal experience, Bursevi says inspiration and address may come in Arabic, Persian, or Turkish without a visible intermediary; divine reception continues until Judgment, though an angel usually mediates unseen.
BURSEVI:v9p236#2/r2.anchor: وقد ذقنا في أنفسنا أنه يجيء الإلهام والخطاب تارة باللفظ العربي وأخرى بالفارسي وبالتركي

THALABI:v1p74/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p74/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p74/r1.claim: Thaʿlabī rejects works that discard isnad, rely on notebooks, and mix sound with poor material; he says learning is passed from elders to juniors and without isnad anyone could say anything.
THALABI:v1p74/r1.anchor: وفرقة حرموا الأسناد الذي هو الركن والعماد، وتملكوا الصحف والدفاتر وجهدوا على ما هو بين الخواطر، وذكروا الغث والسمين، والركيك والمتين

THALABI:v1p74/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p74/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p74/r2.claim: Some accomplished compilers, including al-Tabari and Thaʿlabī’s teacher Ibn Hamid, burden their books with excessive disputes and reports, discouraging seekers; excessive accumulation confuses understanding.
THALABI:v1p74/r2.anchor: وفرقة حازوا قصب السبق في عمدة التصنيف والحذق، غير أنهم طولوا كتبهم بالمعادات، وكثرة الطرق والروايات، وحشوها بما منه بد

THALABI:v1p74/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p74/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p74/r3.claim: Early exegetes such as Mujahid, Muqatil, al-Kalbi, and al-Suddi focused on tafsir but omitted legal rulings, clarification of difficulties, and refutation of deviant arguments; Thaʿlabī still praises their aims.
THALABI:v1p74/r3.anchor: وفرقة جردوا التفسير دون الأحكام، وبيان الحلال من الحرام، والحل عن الغوامض والمشكلات، والرد على أهل الزيغ والشبهات

THALABI:v1p74/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p74/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p74/r4.claim: Finding no comprehensive, polished Quran commentary, and seeing waning interest alongside requests from prominent scholars, Thaʿlabī undertook to serve readers and spread knowledge.
THALABI:v1p74/r4.anchor: فلما لم أعثر في هذا الشأن على كتاب جامع مهذب يعتمد في علم القرآن عليه.. ..، ورأيت رغبة الناس عن هذا العلم ظاهرة

THALABI:v1p74/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p74/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p74/r5.claim: He says he compiled a comprehensive, concise, organized work from more than one hundred tested and heard books, supplemented with other material gathered from nearly three hundred teachers.
THALABI:v1p74/r5.anchor: مستخرج من [نيف و] مائة كتاب مجربات مسموعات، سوى ما التقطته من التطبيقات، والأجزاء المتفرقات وتلقفنه عن أقوام من المشايخ، وهم قريب من ثلاثمائة مستمع

THALABI:v1p74/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p74/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p74/r6.claim: His editorial method is to infer what is closed, collect what is scattered, explain what is obscure, improve organization, and remove or expand material as needed.
THALABI:v1p74/r6.anchor: إما استنباط شيء إن كان مقفلا أو جمعه إن كان متفرقا، أو شرحه إن كان غامضا، أو حسن نظم تأليفه، أو إسقاط شيء وتطويل

THALABI:v1p85#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p85#2/r1.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v1p85#2/r1.claim: Hasan says God wants people to know the circumstances and meaning of every revealed verse.
THALABI:v1p85#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة عن الحسن قال: «والله، ما أنزل الله آية إلا وهو يحب أن نعلم فيم أنزلت، وما معناها»

THALABI:v1p85#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p85#2/r2.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v1p85#2/r2.claim: Hasan says Quranic knowledge is learned only by men.
THALABI:v1p85#2/r2.anchor: وقال الحسن: «علم القرآن لم يعلمه إلا الذكور من الرجال»

THALABI:v1p85#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p85#2/r3.speaker: الفضيل بن العياض
THALABI:v1p85#2/r3.claim: Fudayl rebukes visitors for neglecting the Quran to seek his and Sufyan’s words; Quran study spans generations and requires grammar, clear and ambiguous verses, lawful and unlawful matters, and abrogation, after which other sayings are unnecessary. He cites Yunus 10:57 on its healing.
THALABI:v1p85#2/r3.anchor: الفضيل بن العياض بمكة، فسألناه أن يملي علينا فقال: «ضيعتم كتاب الله وطلبتم كلام فضيل وابن عيينة؟! ولو تفرغتم لكتاب الله تعالى لوجدتم فيه شفاء

THALABI:v1p85#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p85#2/r4.speaker: سفيان الثوري
THALABI:v1p85#2/r4.claim: Sufyan al-Thawri laments spending their lives on legal issues of ila and zihar while leaving God’s Book behind, and asks what they will answer at the resurrection.
THALABI:v1p85#2/r4.anchor: عن سفيان الثوري أنه قال: «أفنينا عمرنا في الإيلاء والظهار ونبذنا كتاب الله وراء ظهورنا فماذا نقول لربنا في المعاد؟»

THALABI:v1p85#2/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p85#2/r5.speaker: البريدي
THALABI:v1p85#2/r5.claim: Al-Buraydi derives tafsir from disclosure and unveiling, relating it to tafsira, a little water doctors inspect to uncover a patient’s illness; likewise an exegete reveals a verse’s context, story, meaning, and occasion.
THALABI:v1p85#2/r5.anchor: سمعت أبا بكر محمد بن الحسن البريدي يقول: [أما التفسير في اللغة فهو راجع إلى معنى الإظهار والكشف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p395/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p395/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p395/r1.claim: Students complained that tafsīr works were enormous and exhausting to produce, hear, or read, yet yielded little benefit to their owners.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p395/r1.anchor: هؤلاء شكوا إلي: غلظ حجم المصنفات في التفسير، وإن الواحدة منها تستغرق (¬7) العمر كتابتها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p395/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p395/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p395/r2.claim: The route to Qurʾānic interpretation is mastering grammar and adab, then studying Arabic metaphors, rare proverbs, similes, unusual wordplay, and concise expressions that carry much meaning.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p395/r2.anchor: فقلت: إن طريق معرفة تفسير كلام الله تعالى تعلم النحو والأدب فإنهما عمدتاه، وإحكام

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p395/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p395/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p395/r3.claim: Al-Wāḥidī laments that people of his time abandoned the effort of learning adab and that its standing had declined.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p395/r3.anchor: وقد أعفى أهل زماننا أنفسهم عن كد التعب في طلب الأدب، فقد هوت (¬1) دولته إلى الحضيض

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p395/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p395/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p395/r4.claim: If adab is lost, people lose what is needed to interpret the Qurʾān, an Arabic book revealed in the Arabs' own language and idiom.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p395/r4.anchor: وإذا ضاع الأدب ضاع ما يحتاج في تفسيره إليه، ويعول في معرفته عليه، وهو علم (¬7) القرآن العربي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p395/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p395/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p395/r5.claim: The first Arabs understood Qurʾānic address through their native eloquence and upbringing, while later non-Arab learners need instruction in difficult vocabulary, figures, and idiom.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p395/r5.anchor: أنزله جل ذكره بلسانهم، وصيغة (¬1) كلامهم الذي نشؤوا (¬2) عليه، وجبلوا على النطق به

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p395/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p395/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p395/r6.claim: The Prophet clarified what the Companions and community needed about the Qurʾān's general, obscure, ambiguous, and other forms; later generations must study Arabic variation and correct usage.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p395/r6.anchor: وبين النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - للمخاطبين من أصحابه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p421/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p421/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p421/r1.claim: Al-Wāḥidī studied Qurʾānic recitation, regional readings, and imams' selections with ʿAlī al-Bustī through many complete readings, including much of Ibn Mihrān's method.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p421/r1.anchor: وقرأت عليه القرآن ختمات كثيرة لا تحصى، حتى قرأت عليه أكثر طريقة الأستاذ

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p421/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p421/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p421/r2.claim: He studied with Saʿīd al-Ḥīrī and ʿAlī al-Fārisī, whom he describes as senior authorities with many teachers and students, abundant knowledge, elevated transmission, and reliability.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p421/r2.anchor: وكانا قد انتهت إليهما الرئاسة في هذا العلم، وأشير إليهما بالأصابع في علو السن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p421/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p421/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p421/r3.claim: With Saʿīd he read Ibn Mihrān's works and received books by Abū ʿAlī al-Fasawī; he also read al-Zajjāj's Maʿānī through Ibn Miqsam's transmission.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p421/r3.anchor: وقرأت على الأستاذ (سعيد) مصنفات ابن مهران (¬2)، وروى لنا كتب أبي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p421/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p421/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p421/r4.claim: Al-Wāḥidī then studied extensively with al-Thaʿlabī, author of al-Kashf wa-l-Bayān, whose achievement he says all communities recognized; he read over five hundred parts of his works.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p421/r4.anchor: ثم فرغت للأستاذ الإمام "أبي إسحاق أحمد بن محمد بن إبراهيم الثعلبي" رحمه الله

BURHAN:v1p179/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p179/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p179/r1.claim: Zarkashi classifies declarative clauses as a type of sūra opening, listing al-Anbiya, al-Qamar and al-Rahman among twenty-three such sūras.
BURHAN:v1p179/r1.anchor: الرابع الجمل الخبرية نحو ﴿ يسألونك عن الأنفال ﴾ ﴿ براءة من الله ﴾

BURHAN:v1p312/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p312/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p312/r1.claim: Knowledge of rhetoric's forms is central to exegesis and eloquence; the author says God's teaching of the Qur'an and human speech alone would suffice to show the honor of eloquence.
BURHAN:v1p312/r1.anchor: واعلم أن معرفة هذه الصناعة بأوضاعها هى عمدة التفسير المطلع على عجائب كلام الله وهى قاعدة الفصاحة وواسطة عقد البلاغة

BURHAN:v1p312/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p312/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p312/r2.claim: The author invokes “This is a clear statement for people” and “a clarification of all things” as further scriptural praise of البيان.
BURHAN:v1p312/r2.anchor: وقال تعالى ﴿ هذا بيان للناس ﴾ وقال تعالى ﴿ تبيانا لكل شيء ﴾

BURHAN:v3p448/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p448/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
BURHAN:v3p448/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari reports that Amr ibn Ubayd read “a rose like oil” in the nominative, as though a rose-colored sky emerged from it, and classifies the expression as tajrid.
BURHAN:v3p448/r4.anchor: وذكر الزمخشري أن عمرو بن عبيد قرأ في قوله تعالى ﴿ فكانت وردة كالدهان ﴾ 2 بالرفع

BURHAN:v1p4/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p4/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p4/r1.claim: The Qur'an is inexhaustibly rich in benefits and meanings, beyond the complete comprehension of human understanding or eloquence.
BURHAN:v1p4/r1.anchor: فسبحان من سلكه ينابيع في القلوب

BURHAN:v1p4/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p4/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p4/r2.claim: The Qur'an is called a spirit because it brings enduring life to the heart, serving as a means of ability and a sign for reflection.
BURHAN:v1p4/r2.anchor: يحيي القلوب بأوراده ، ولهذا سماه الله روحا

BURHAN:v1p4/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p4/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p4/r3.claim: Understanding the Qur'an's meanings and secrets requires strong insight, sustained thought, refined disposition, and command of Arabic literary arts.
BURHAN:v1p4/r3.anchor: وإنما يفهم بعض معانيه ، ويطلع على أسراره ومبانيه

BURHAN:v1p4/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p4/r4.speaker: الحرالي
BURHAN:v1p4/r4.claim: Al-Ḥarālī says divine gifts enable learning; the most complete scholars receive understanding and insight into the Qur'an, which encompasses all sciences.

BURHAN:v1p4/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p4/r5.speaker: الشافعي
BURHAN:v1p4/r5.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī describes the community's statements as explaining the Sunna, the Sunna as explaining the Qur'an, and the Qur'an as explaining God's names and attributes.
BURHAN:v1p4/r5.anchor: وقال الشافعي رضي الله عنه : جميع ما تقوله الأمة شرح للسنة

BURHAN:v1p4/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p4/r6.speaker: غيره
BURHAN:v1p4/r6.claim: Another authority adds that the beautiful names all explain God's greatest name.
BURHAN:v1p4/r6.anchor: زاد غيره : وجميع الأسماء الحسنى شرح لاسمه الأعظم

BURHAN:v1p4/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p4/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p4/r7.claim: Because the Qur'an is superior to other speech, its sciences surpass other disciplines; the author cites 39:9 and 2:269.
BURHAN:v1p4/r7.anchor: وكما أنه أفضل من كل كلام سواه ، فعلومه أفضل من كل علم عداه

BURHAN:v1p4/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p4/r8.speaker: مجاهد
BURHAN:v1p4/r8.claim: Mujāhid glosses the wisdom granted in 2:269 as understanding and sound judgment in the Qur'an.
BURHAN:v1p4/r8.anchor: قال مجاهد : الفهم والإصابة في القرآن

BURHAN:v1p4/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p4/r9.speaker: مقاتل
BURHAN:v1p4/r9.claim: Muqātil glosses the wisdom in 2:269 as knowledge of the Qur'an.

BURHAN:v2p24/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p24/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p24/r1.claim: The Qur'an contains every kind of proof, demonstration, division, and definition concerning universal rational and transmitted knowledge.
BURHAN:v2p24/r1.anchor: اعلم أن القرآن العظيم قد اشتمل على جميع أنواع البراهين والأدلة وما من برهان ودلالة وتقسيم وتحديد

BURHAN:v2p24/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p24/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p24/r2.claim: God presents arguments in the Arabs' customary idiom, consistent with the principle that each messenger speaks his people's language.
BURHAN:v2p24/r2.anchor: ما أرسلنا من رسول إلا بلسان قومه

BURHAN:v2p24/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p24/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p24/r3.claim: Turning to obscure disputational detail can signal inability to establish a point plainly; the Qur'an instead gives proof in the clearest effective form.
BURHAN:v2p24/r3.anchor: هو العاجز عن إقامة الحجة بالجليل من الكلام

BURHAN:v2p24/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p24/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p24/r4.claim: Qur'anic argument addresses ordinary listeners through clear reasoning while allowing specialists to discern subtleties beyond ordinary orators' understanding.
BURHAN:v2p24/r4.anchor: لتفهم العامة من جليلها ما يقنعهم ويلزمهم الحجة وتفهم الخواص من أثنائها ما يوفي على ما أدركه فهم الخطباء

BURHAN:v2p24/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p24/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p24/r5.claim: The author reads the report that each verse has an outer and inner sense, and each letter a limit and an opening, as describing layered comprehension, not Batini esotericism.

BURHAN:v2p24/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p24/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p24/r6.claim: A person's share of Qur'anic knowledge grows with their share of learning; its proofs address rational people, listeners, thinkers, and those who remember.
BURHAN:v2p24/r6.anchor: كل من كان حظه في العلوم أوفر كان نصيبه من علم القرآن أكثر

BURHAN:v2p24/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p24/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p24/r7.claim: God attributes signs of His lordship and oneness in different passages to reasoning, hearing, reflection, and recollection, indicating different faculties can apprehend them.
BURHAN:v2p24/r7.anchor: تنبيها أن بكل قوة من هذه القوى يمكن إدراك حقيقته منها

BURHAN:v2p24/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p24/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p24/r8.claim: The Qur'an supplies rational evidence for the world's origination: changing qualities and transitions between states indicate that it came to be.
BURHAN:v2p24/r8.anchor: الاستدلال على حدوث العالم بتغير الصفات عليه وانتقاله من حال إلى حال وهو آية الحدوث

BURHAN:v2p24/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p24/r9.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p24/r9.claim: Abraham's argument from the setting heavenly bodies moves from the origination of lesser bodies to a creator and extends the proof to all bodies because they share corporeality.
BURHAN:v2p24/r9.anchor: استدلاله بحدوث الأقل على وجود المحدث والحكم على السماوات والأرض بحكم النيرات الثلاث

BURHAN:v2p154/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p154/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
BURHAN:v2p154/r1.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says that anyone seeking knowledge of earlier and later peoples should deeply investigate the Qur'an.
BURHAN:v2p154/r1.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود من اراد علم الأولين والآخرين فليثور القرآن

BURHAN:v2p154/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p154/r2.speaker: ابن سبع
BURHAN:v2p154/r2.claim: Ibn Sabʿ says the claims of Abū al-Dardāʾ and Ibn Masʿūd are not realized by surface commentary alone.
BURHAN:v2p154/r2.anchor: قال ابن سبع في شفاء الصدور هذا الذي قاله أبو الدرداء وابن مسعود لا يحصل بمجرد تفسير الظاهر

BURHAN:v2p154/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p154/r3.speaker: بعض العلماء
BURHAN:v2p154/r3.claim: Some scholars estimate that each verse has sixty thousand understandings, with still more remaining beyond that.
BURHAN:v2p154/r3.anchor: وقد قال بعض العلماء لكل آية ستون الف فهم وما بقي من فهمها اكثر

BURHAN:v2p154/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p154/r4.speaker: قول آخر
BURHAN:v2p154/r4.claim: Another estimate says the Qur'an contains 77,200 sciences, multiplying each word's knowledge fourfold as outer, inner, limit, and opening.
BURHAN:v2p154/r4.anchor: وقال آخر القرآن يحوي سبعة وسبعين الف علم ومائتي علم اذ لكل كلمة علم ثم يتضاعف ذلك اربعة

BURHAN:v2p154/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p154/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p154/r5.claim: All sciences concern God's acts and attributes, which the Qur'an explains; its meanings therefore have vast scope.
BURHAN:v2p154/r5.anchor: فالعلوم كلها داخلة في افعال الله تعالى وصفاته وفي القرآن شرح ذاته وصفاته وأفعاله

BURHAN:v2p154/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p154/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p154/r6.claim: Transmitted surface exegesis is necessary to avoid error, but later understanding and inference can expand; rare meanings require broad learning and listening.
BURHAN:v2p154/r6.anchor: المنقول من ظاهر التفسير ليس ينتهي الإدراك فيه بالنقل والسماع لا بد منه في ظاهر التفسير ليتقي به مواضع الغلط

BURHAN:v2p154/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p154/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p154/r7.claim: One must master the apparent meaning before seeking inner meanings; claiming Qur'anic secrets without surface exegesis is like claiming to reach a room without passing through the door.
BURHAN:v2p154/r7.anchor: انه لايجوز التهاون بحفظ التفسير الظاهر اولا ولا مطمع

BURHAN:v2p154/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p154/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p154/r8.claim: Since the Qur'an was revealed in Arabic, understanding its words requires learning Arabic or most of it; human understanding cannot exhaust God's speech.
BURHAN:v2p154/r8.anchor: فظاهر التفسير يجري مجرى تعلم اللغة التي لا بد منها للفهم وما لا بد فيها من استماع كثير

BURHAN:v2p154/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p154/r9.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p154/r9.claim: Without knowledge, understanding, piety, and reflection, a person cannot experience the Qur'an's delight.
BURHAN:v2p154/r9.anchor: ومن لم يكن له علم وفهم وتقوى وتدبر لم يدرك من لذة القرآن شيئا

BURHAN:v2p154/r10.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p154/r10.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p154/r10.claim: The statement both affirms and denies the Prophet's throwing: he threw in one respect, while what God caused to occur was not his act in another respect.
BURHAN:v2p154/r10.anchor: فإنه اثبات للرمي ونفي له وهما متضادان في الظاهر مالم يفهم انه رمى من وجه ولم يرم من جهة

BURHAN:v2p172/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p172/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p172/r1.claim: When no transmitted interpretation exists, determine a word's meaning from Arabic usage and context; al-Rāghib often adds a contextual qualification beyond lexicographers.
BURHAN:v2p172/r1.anchor: وطريق التوصل إلى فهمه النظر إلى مفردات الألفاظ من لغة العرب ومدلولاتها واستعمالها بحسب السياق وهذا يعتني به الراغب كثيرا

BURHAN:v2p172/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p172/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p172/r2.claim: An exegete should begin with verbal sciences and establish the meanings of individual Qur'anic words before composing interpretation.
BURHAN:v2p172/r2.anchor: الذي يجب على المفسر البداءة به العلوم اللفظية وأول ما يجب البداءة به منها تحقيق الألفاظ المفردة

BURHAN:v2p172/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p172/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p172/r3.claim: A compound cannot be known before its parts; the same priority of individual words applies across religious and other fields of knowledge.
BURHAN:v2p172/r3.anchor: المركب لايعلم الا بعد العلم بمفرداته لأن الجزء سابق على الكل في الوجود

BURHAN:v2p172/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p172/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p172/r4.claim: Individual-word study covers lexical meanings, the forms and patterns that convey different meanings, and the derivation of branches from roots.
BURHAN:v2p172/r4.anchor: وأما بحسب الأفراد فمن وجوه ثلاثة من جهة المعاني التي وضعت الألفاظ المفردة بإزائها

BURHAN:v2p172/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p172/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p172/r5.claim: For compounds, syntax studies grammatical arrangement and the core meaning conveyed by that arrangement.
BURHAN:v2p172/r5.anchor: الأول باعتبار كيفية التراكيب بحسب الإعراب ومقابله من حيث انها مؤدية اصل المعنى

BURHAN:v2p172/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p172/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p172/r6.claim: The science of meanings studies implications beyond a construction's basic meaning as determined by rhetorical context.
BURHAN:v2p172/r6.anchor: الثاني باعتبار كيفية التركيب من جهة افادته معنى المعنى اعني لازم اصل المعنى الذي يختلف باختلاف مقتضى الحال

BURHAN:v2p172/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p172/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p172/r7.claim: The science of bayan studies clarity and ranks of indication, including literal and figurative speech, metaphor, metonymy, and simile.
BURHAN:v2p172/r7.anchor: الثالث باعتبار طرق تأدية المقصود بحسب وضوح الدلالة وحقائقها ومراتبها وباعتبار الحقيقة والمجاز والاستعارة والكناية والتشبيه

ITQAN:v4p342/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p342/r1.speaker: الشيخ عز الدين
ITQAN:v4p342/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbd al-Salam lists indicators of permissibility, including permission, removal of blame, benefit, allowance, and silence about prohibition; praise alongside such a report indicates obligation or recommendation.
ITQAN:v4p342/r1.anchor: وتستفاد الإباحة من لفظ الإحلال ونفي الجناح والحرج والإثم والمؤاخذة ومن الإذن فيه والعفو عنه

ITQAN:v4p342/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p342/r2.speaker: جماعة
ITQAN:v4p342/r2.claim: Some argue that the Qur'an is uncreated: scripture calls the human created in eighteen places but never calls the Qur'an created in fifty-four, and distinguishes teaching the Qur'an from creating humanity.
ITQAN:v4p342/r2.anchor: وقد استدل جماعة على أن القرآن غير مخلوق بأن الله ذكر الإنسان في ثمانية عشر موضعا وقال إنه مخلوق

ITQAN:v4p343/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p343/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p343/r1.claim: Al-Mawardi, a leading Shafiʿi scholar, wrote a dedicated work on Qur'anic parables, which the Qur'an says are given for people to reflect on.
ITQAN:v4p343/r1.anchor: أفرده بالتصنيف الإمام أبو الحسن الماوردي من كبار أصحابنا قال تعالى

ITQAN:v4p343/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p343/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
ITQAN:v4p343/r2.claim: Abu Hurayra reports a prophetic saying that the Qur'an came in five forms: lawful, unlawful, clear, ambiguous, and parables; act on the lawful, avoid the unlawful, follow the clear, believe the ambiguous, and learn from parables.
ITQAN:v4p343/r2.anchor: أخرج البيهقي عن أبي هريرة قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

ITQAN:v4p343/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p343/r3.speaker: الماوردي
ITQAN:v4p343/r3.claim: Al-Mawardi calls knowledge of parables one of the greatest Qur'anic sciences, but says people neglect it by attending to the examples while ignoring what they represent; an unrepresented parable is like an unbridled horse or unhaltered camel.
ITQAN:v4p343/r3.anchor: قال الماوردي من أعظم علم القرآن علم أمثاله والناس في غفلة عنه لاشتغالهم بالأمثال وإغفالهم الممثلات

ITQAN:v4p343/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p343/r4.speaker: الشافعي
ITQAN:v4p343/r4.claim: Al-Shafiʿi counts knowledge of parables that indicate obedience and warn against disobedience among the Qur'anic sciences a jurist must know.
ITQAN:v4p343/r4.anchor: قد عده الشافعي مما يجب على المجتهد معرفته من علوم القرآن فقال ثم معرفة ما ضرب فيه من الأمثال

ITQAN:v4p343/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p343/r5.speaker: الشيخ عز الدين
ITQAN:v4p343/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbd al-Salam says parables serve remembrance and admonition; when they show degrees of reward, wasted deeds, praise, or blame, they indicate legal rulings.
ITQAN:v4p343/r5.anchor: إنما ضرب الله الأمثال في القرآن تذكيرا ووعظا فما اشتمل منها على تفاوت في ثواب أو على إحباط عمل

ITQAN:v4p343/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p343/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p343/r6.claim: Parables exhort, deter, prompt reflection, reinforce, clarify meaning, and make abstract matters sensory and memorable by comparing the hidden to the clear and the absent to the witnessed; they also establish or refute claims and convey reward, punishment, praise, blame, and degrees of importance.
ITQAN:v4p343/r6.anchor: ضرب الأمثال في القرآن يستفاد منه أمور كثيرة التذكير والوعظ والحث والزجر والاعتبار والتقرير

ITQAN:v4p343/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p343/r7.speaker: الزركشي
ITQAN:v4p343/r7.claim: Al-Zarkashi says one wisdom of Qur'anic parables is teaching eloquence, a distinctive feature of this religious law.
ITQAN:v4p343/r7.anchor: وقال الزركشي في البرهان ومن حكمته تعليم البيان وهو من خصائص هذه الشريعة

ITQAN:v4p343/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p343/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
ITQAN:v4p343/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says analogy reveals meanings and brings conjectural ideas close to what is witnessed; the comparison should match the greatness or lowliness of what it represents.
ITQAN:v4p343/r8.anchor: وقال الزمخشري التمثيل إنما يصار إليه لكشف المعاني وإدناء المتوهم من الشاهد

ITQAN:v4p493/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p493/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p493/r1.claim: Ten Companions were especially known for Qur'anic exegesis: the four caliphs, Ibn Masʿud, Ibn ʿAbbas, Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, Zayd ibn Thabit, Abu Musa al-Ashʿari, and ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zubayr.
ITQAN:v4p493/r1.anchor: اشتهر بالتفسير من الصحابة عشرة الخلفاء الأربعة وابن مسعود وابن عباس وأبي بن كعب

ITQAN:v4p493/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p493/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p493/r2.claim: Among the caliphs, most tafsir reports come from ʿAli; reports from the other three are scarce, likely because they died earlier, and fewer than ten tafsir reports are known from Abu Bakr.
ITQAN:v4p493/r2.anchor: أما الخلفاء فأكثر من روي عنه منهم علي بن أبي طالب والرواية عن الثلاثة نزرة جدا وكأن السبب في ذلك تقدم وفاتهم

ITQAN:v4p493/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p493/r3.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
ITQAN:v4p493/r3.claim: ʿAli invited questions about the Qur'an and said he knew of every verse whether it was revealed by night or day, on a plain or a mountain; Abu al-Tufayl reports this sermon.
ITQAN:v4p493/r3.anchor: قال شهدت عليا يخطب وهو يقول

ITQAN:v4p493/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p493/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
ITQAN:v4p493/r4.claim: Ibn Masʿud reports that the Qur'an came in seven readings, each with an outward and inward sense, and that ʿAli knew both.
ITQAN:v4p493/r4.anchor: وأخرج أبو نعيم في الحلية عن ابن مسعود قال إن القرآن أنزل على سبعة أحرف ما منها حرف إلا وله ظهر وبطن

ITQAN:v4p493/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p493/r5.speaker: علي
ITQAN:v4p493/r5.claim: ʿAli swore that he knew the circumstances and place of revelation of every verse, saying God gave him an understanding heart and an inquisitive tongue.
ITQAN:v4p493/r5.anchor: عن علي قال والله ما نزلت آية إلا وقد علمت فيم أنزلت وأين أنزلت إن ربي وهب لي قلبا عقولا

ITQAN:v4p493/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p493/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p493/r6.claim: Al-Suyuti reports Ibn Masʿud saying he knew the audience and place of revelation for every verse and would travel to anyone who knew the Qur'an better than he did.
ITQAN:v4p493/r6.anchor: ما نزلت آية من كتاب الله إلا وأنا أعلم فيمن نزلت وأين نزلت

ITQAN:v4p493/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p493/r7.speaker: أبو البختري
ITQAN:v4p493/r7.claim: Abu al-Bakhtari reports that ʿAli praised Ibn Masʿud as learned in the Qur'an and Sunna, saying that was sufficient knowledge.
ITQAN:v4p493/r7.anchor: وأخرج أبو نعيم عن أبي البختري قال قالوا لعلي أخبرنا عن ابن مسعود قال علم القرآن والسنة

ITQAN:v4p493/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p493/r8.speaker: ابن عمر
ITQAN:v4p493/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas was known as the Qur'an's interpreter, and the Prophet prayed for his understanding of religion, knowledge of interpretation and wisdom; Ibn ʿUmar reports another prayer for blessing and spreading his influence.
ITQAN:v4p493/r8.anchor: وأخرج أبو نعيم في الحلية عن ابن عمر قال دعا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p1/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p1/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p1/r1.claim: Speech gives knowledge its ranks, reveals its forms and inner meanings, and allows its fruits to be shared; the opening of al-Rahman illustrates this divine teaching.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p1/r1.anchor: الكلام هو الذي يعطي العلوم منازلها ويبين مراتبها ويكشف عن صورها ويجني صنوف ثمرها

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p1/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p1/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p1/r2.claim: God distinguishes humans from other animals through speech, which the author presents as a great divine favor.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p1/r2.anchor: وبه أبان الله تعالى الإنسان من سائر الحيوان ونبه فيه على عظم الامتنان

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p1/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p1/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p1/r3.claim: Without speech, knowledge and thought would remain trapped within their possessors, and people could not distinguish faith from unbelief or praise from blame.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p1/r3.anchor: ولبقيت القلوب مقفلة على ودائعها والمعاني مسجونة في مواضعها

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p1/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p1/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p1/r4.claim: Speech’s special function is to present what is known with the qualities and states that knowledge has found in it.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p1/r4.anchor: أنه يريك المعلومات بأوصافها التي وجدها العلم عليها ويقرر كيفياتها التي تناولها المعرفة

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p1/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p1/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p1/r5.claim: The best speech most fully realizes this distinctive function; excellence does not lie in isolated words but in their particular composition and order.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p1/r5.anchor: والألفاظ لا تفيد حتى تؤلف ضربا خاصا من التأليف ويعمد بها إلى وجه دون وجه من التركيب والترتيب

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p589/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p589/r6.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p589/r6.claim: Before the refrain, the surah has already commanded the accountable humans and jinn about justice in weighing and taught them the Qur'an; the address therefore follows established context.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p589/r6.anchor: قبل الآية الأولى فيها خطاب المكلفين وهما الإنس والجن

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1044/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1044/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1044/r1.claim: The Qur'an is named before human creation because it is the book of worship, and worship is the purpose for which humans and jinn were created; purpose precedes the work it governs.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1044/r1.anchor: فلما كان خلق الإنسان والجن لغرض العبادة والقرآن هو كتاب العبادة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1044/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1044/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1044/r2.claim: The Qur'an, as God's speech and part of His knowledge, already existed before the human being; it thus precedes creation in existence as well as purpose.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1044/r2.anchor: القرآن كلام الله ومن علم الله وهو موجود قبل الإنسان

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1044/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1044/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1044/r3.claim: The Qur'an is prior in purpose, existence, and merit; Qur'anic order need not be chronological and may instead follow context, priority, or excellence, sometimes placing a later event first.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1044/r3.anchor: إذا كان على الفضل هو أسبق وإذا كان على الزمن هو أسبق وإذا كان على العلة والغرض هو أسبق

ALUSI-FULL:v1p9/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p9/r1.speaker: ساداتنا الصوفية
ALUSI-FULL:v1p9/r1.claim: They interpret the Merciful’s teaching of the Quran as a merciful self-disclosure that gives the servant a Quranic knowing and delight; God is known only through His names and attributes.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p9/r1.anchor: فهو إشارة إلى أن العبد إذا تجلى عليه الرحمن وجد لذة رحمانية تكسبه معرفة قرآنية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p227#3/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p227#3/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p227#3/r8.claim: A second reported occasion is the claim that a human taught Muhammad; the sura replies that the All-Merciful taught him the Quran.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p227#3/r8.anchor: وقيل سبب نزولها قول المشركين إنما يعلمه بشر المحكي في سورة النحل . فرد الله عليهم بأن الرحمن هو الذي علم النبي القرآن .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p227#3/r15.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p227#3/r15.speaker: الكشاف
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p227#3/r15.claim: The Kashshaf says the sura leads with the greatest religious favor, Quranic revelation and teaching, then human creation and the distinctive gift of expression.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p227#3/r15.anchor: قال في ( الكشاف ) : ( أراد الله أن يقدم في عدد آلائه أول شيء ما هو أسبق قدما من ضروب آلائه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p229/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p229/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p229/r1.claim: The sura honors the Prophet by saying God taught him the Quran, answering the pagans' claim that a human taught him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p229/r1.anchor: وتبع ذلك من التنويه بالنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بأن الله هو الذي علمه القرآن ردا على مزاعم المشركين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p229/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p229/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p229/r2.claim: This also answers the claims that the Quran is ancient fables, magic, soothsayer speech, or poetry.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p229/r2.anchor: وردا على مزاعمهم أن القرآن أساطير الأولين أو أنه سحر أو كلام كاهن أو شعر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p229/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p229/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p229/r10.claim: Most verse counters treat the opening as one verse.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p229/r10.anchor: هذه آية واحدة عند جمهور العادين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p231/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p231/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p231/r1.claim: Al-Quran is the second object of the doubled verb allama, which here takes two objects and denotes imparting instruction.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p231/r1.anchor: وانتصب { القرآن } على أنه مفعول ثان لفعل { علم }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p231/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p231/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p231/r2.claim: Ma'n ibn Aws's line about teaching archery, alongside Quran 5:110 and 36:69, illustrates teaching a discipline or thing; form IV aʿlama instead reports information to someone.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p231/r2.anchor: فهو كقول معن بن أوس : أعلمه الرماية كل يوم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p231/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p231/r3.speaker: author
