IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p231/r3.claim: The doubled form of allama yields instruction, unlike the hamza form aʿlama, which conveys informing or announcing.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p231/r3.anchor: ففعل علم إذا ضعف كان بمعنى تحصيل التعليم بخلافه إذ عدي بالهمزة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p231/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p231/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p231/r4.claim: The sura counts great worldly favors for all and afterlife favors for believers, and leads with religion because it reforms worldly life and brings success in the next.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p231/r4.anchor: وقد عدد الله في هذه السورة نعما عظيمة على الناس كلهم في الدنيا ، وعلى المؤمنين خاصة في الآخرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p231/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p231/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p231/r5.claim: Islam is the best religion and the revelation for this age; since it comes through the best divine revelation, the Quran is named first and signals Islam and earlier religions' favors.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p231/r5.anchor: ولما كان دين الإسلام أفضل الأديان ، وكان هو المنزل للناس في هذا الإبان ، وكان متلقى من أفضل الوحي والكتب الإلهية وهو القرآن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p231/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p231/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p231/r7.claim: Al-Quran is the established name for the verbal revelation to Muhammad, whose wording is recited as worship and whose inimitability extends to a single sura.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p231/r7.anchor: و { القرآن } : اسم غلب على الوحي اللفظي الذي أوحي به إلى محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم للإعجاز بسورة منه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p12/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p12/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p12/r1.claim: Some interpretations are not propositions: identifying the Day of Judgment is a verbal definition, while inferring a six-month minimum pregnancy from two verses is an implication.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p12/r1.anchor: لم يكن شيء من ذلك قضية ، بل الأول تعريف لفظي ، والثاني من دلالة الالتزام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p12/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p12/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p12/r2.claim: First, tafsir yields many sciences and universal rules, so its discussions can be treated like the principles they generate; preserving poetry is likewise called a science because it supports linguistic and rhetorical discoveries.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p12/r2.anchor: نزلت منزلة القواعد الكلية لأنها مبدأ لها ، ومنشأ

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p12/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p12/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p12/r3.claim: Second, requiring universal propositions applies to rational disciplines, not religious and literary fields; a discipline qualifies if studying it improves knowledge, and tafsir does this supremely by explaining God’s intent.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p12/r3.anchor: أما العلوم الشرعية والأدبية فلا يشترط فيها ذلك ، بل يكفي أن تكون مباحثها مفيدة كمالا علميا لمزاولها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p12/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p12/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p12/r4.claim: Third, some scholars regard verbal definitions as assertions reducible to propositions; the abundant meanings derived from them and Arabic poetry used as evidence function like proofs.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p12/r4.anchor: التعاريف اللفظية تصديقات على رأي بعض المحققين فهي تؤول إلى قضايا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p12/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p12/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p12/r5.claim: Fourth, tafsir contains universal rules within it, including principles of abrogation, interpretation, and decisive verses; Ibn Faris, al-Suyuti, and al-Kafawi collected Qur’anic universals.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p12/r5.anchor: إن علم التفسير لا يخلو من قواعد كلية في أثنائه مثل تقرير قواعد النسخ عند تفسير ) ما ننسخ من آية (

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p12/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p12/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p12/r6.claim: Fifth, tafsir ought to explain the foundations and general principles of legislation, but exegetes were overwhelmed by the detailed meanings and extracted such principles only occasionally.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p12/r6.anchor: أن حق التفسير أن يشتمل على بيان أصول التشريع وكلياته فكان بذلك حقيقا بأن يسمى علما

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p12/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p12/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p12/r7.claim: Sixth, tafsir was the first Islamic discipline studied and debated; practice gave scholars a trained grasp of Qur’anic styles and subtle composition, yielding general knowledge specific to the Qur’an. Ibn Ashur calls this decisive.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p12/r7.anchor: السادس وهو الفصل : أن التفسير كان أول ما اشتغل به علماء الإسلام قبل الاشتغال بتدوين بقية العلوم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p12/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p12/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p12/r8.claim: As explanation of God’s intended meaning, tafsir is a principal religious science in al-Ghazali’s scheme and the head of Islamic sciences as al-Baydawi describes it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p12/r8.anchor: كان معدودا من أصول العلوم الشرعية وهي التي ذكرها الغزالي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p12/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p12/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p12/r9.claim: When viewed as the study of Meccan and Medinan revelation, abrogation, readings, interpretation, and legal method, tafsir belongs among al-Ghazali’s supplementary religious sciences rather than the principal sciences.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p12/r9.anchor: كان معدودا في متممات العلوم الشرعية المذكورة في الضرب الرابع من كلام الغزالي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p60#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p60#2/r1.speaker: أبو بكر بن العربي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p60#2/r1.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says readings compatible with the Uthmanic codex are mutawatir even when delivery and pronunciation differ, because their transmission follows the mass-transmitted written consonantal form.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p60#2/r1.anchor: التي لا تخالف الألفاظ التي كتبت في مصحف عثمان هي متواترة وإن اختلفت في وجوه الأداء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p60#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p60#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p60#2/r2.claim: Ibn Ashur distinguishes the mass-transmitted Uthmanic text from variant vocalizations: forms compatible with its script are accepted, while the individual variant forms are not themselves all mutawatir.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p60#2/r2.anchor: وما كان نطقه صالحا لرسم المصحف ، واختلف فيه فهو مقبول ، وما هو بمتواتر لأن وجود الاختلاف فيه مناف لدعوى التواتر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p60#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p60#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p60#2/r3.claim: Readings outside the Uthmanic codex, such as what is transmitted from Ibn Masud, fall outside this acceptance; Companion-era Muslim use without objection made the accepted variants collectively mutawatir by choice, though their named chains are singular.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p60#2/r3.anchor: فخرج بذلك ما كان من القراءات مخالفا لمصحف عثمان ، مثل ما نقل من قراءة ابن مسعود ، ولما قرأ المسلمون بهذه القراءات من عصر الصحابة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p60#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p60#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p60#2/r4.claim: Ibn Ashur rejects the notion that all readings, including their transmitters’ methods and recensions, are mutawatir: their listed chains are solitary, with Nafi’s among the strongest because it has two Companion transmitters.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p60#2/r4.anchor: وليس المراد ما يتوهمه بعض القراء من أن القراءات كلها بما فيها من طرائق أصحابها ورواياتهم متواترة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p60#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p60#2/r5.speaker: الأبياري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p60#2/r5.claim: Ibn al-Arabi, Ibn Abd al-Salam al-Tunisi, Ibn Idris, and al-Abyari hold that the readings are not mutawatir; Ibn Ashur endorses their view because the chains prove only that named readers differed, while the Qur’anic wording itself is established independently.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p60#2/r5.anchor: والأبياري من الشافعية بأنها غير متواترة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p60#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p60#2/r6.speaker: إمام الحرمين
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p60#2/r6.claim: Imam al-Haramayn says the readings are mutawatir; al-Abyari rejects his position.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p60#2/r6.anchor: وقال إمام الحرمين في البرهان : هي متواترة ورده عليه الأبياري ، وقال المازري

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p60#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p60#2/r7.speaker: المازري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p60#2/r7.claim: Al-Maziri offers a middle position: the readings are mutawatir among specialists in recitation, but not among the Muslim community at large.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p60#2/r7.anchor: وقال المازري في شرحه : هي متواترة عند القراء وليست متواترة عند عموم الأمة ، وهذا توسط

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p60#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p60#2/r8.speaker: ابن سلامة الأنصاري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p60#2/r8.claim: Ibn Salama al-Ansari, a Maliki, agrees with Imam al-Haramayn that the readings are mutawatir.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p60#2/r8.anchor: ووافق إمام الحرمين ابن سلامة الأنصاري من المالكية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p60#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p60#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p60#2/r9.claim: The transmission question was the subject of an important exchange between Ibn Arafa al-Tunisi and Ibn Lab al-Andalusi, recorded by al-Wansharisi in al-Mi‘yar.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p60#2/r9.anchor: وهذه مسألة مهمة جرى فيها حوار بين الشيخين ابن عرفة التونسي وابن لب الأندلسي ذكرها الونشريسي في المعيار

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p60#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p60#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p60#2/r10.claim: The ten reading traditions trace back to eight Companions: Umar, Uthman, Ali, Ibn Masud, Ubayy ibn Kab, Abu al-Darda, Zayd ibn Thabit, and Abu Musa al-Ashari; individual readings trace to some or all of them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p60#2/r10.anchor: وتنتهي أسانيد القراءات العشر إلى ثمانية من الصحابة وهم : عمر بن الخطاب ، وعثمان ابن عفان ، وعلي ابن أبي طالب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p60#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p60#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p60#2/r11.claim: Most Qur’anic syntactic parses are mutawatir; exceptions allow two parses with the same meaning, such as reading “wa-lata hina” with hina accusative or nominative and “hatta yaqula” with yaqula subjunctive or indicative.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p60#2/r11.anchor: فأكثرها متواتر إلا ما ساغ فيه إعرابان مع اتحاد المعاني نحو ) ولات حين مناص ( بنصب حين ورفعه ، ونحو

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p60#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p60#2/r12.speaker: بعض المعتزلة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p60#2/r12.claim: Although the community agrees that “Allah” is nominative in “God spoke to Moses,” some Mu‘tazilites read it accusative to avoid affirming speech as an attribute of God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p60#2/r12.anchor: ألا ترى أن الأمة أجمعت على رفع اسم الجلالة في قوله تعالى ) وكلم الله موسى تكليما ( وقرأه بعض المعتزلة بنصب اسم الجلالة لئلا يثبتوا لله كلاما

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p60#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p60#2/r13.speaker: بعض الرافضة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p60#2/r13.claim: Ibn Ashur condemns a reading attributed to some Rafidis that makes “the misleaders” dual and interprets them as Abu Bakr and Umar.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p60#2/r13.anchor: وقرأ بعض الرافضة ) وما كنت متخذ المضلين عضدا ( بصيغة التثنية ، وفسروها بأبي بكر وعمر حاشاهما

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p60#2/r14.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p60#2/r14.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p60#2/r14.claim: Ibn Ashur rejects dismissing mass-transmitted readings as bad Arabic merely because they depart from Basran or Kufan grammatical norms; there is no proof those schools exhaust eloquent Arabic.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p60#2/r14.anchor: لأنا لا ثقة لنا بانحصار فصيح كلام العرب فيما صار إلى نحاة البصرة والكوفة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p60#2/r15.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p60#2/r15.speaker: الزمخشري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p60#2/r15.claim: Al-Zamakhshari disqualifies several mutawatir readings as grammatically weak; Ibn Ashur highlights Ibn Amir’s passive “zuyyina” reading, with “qatlu” nominative, “awladahum” accusative, and “shuraka'ihim” genitive.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p60#2/r15.anchor: ما زيفه الزمخشري من القراءات المتواترة بعلة أنها جرت على وجوه ضعيفة في العربية لا سيما ما كان منه في قراءة مشهورة كقراءة عبد الله بن عامر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p60#2/r16.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p60#2/r16.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p60#2/r16.claim: Even a less-preferred grammatical form is a variation in pronunciation that does not negate transmission; alternate case assignment and passive versus active voice can carry distinct meanings and rhetorical effects.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p60#2/r16.anchor: ولو سلمنا أن ذلك وجه مرجوح ، فهو لا يعدو أن يكون من الاختلاف في كيفية النطق التي لا تناكد التواتر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p60#2/r17.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p60#2/r17.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p60#2/r17.claim: Abu Ali al-Farisi wrote al-Hujja to defend transmitted readings on grammatical grounds.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p60#2/r17.anchor: على أن أبا علي الفارسي ألف كتابا سماه الحجة احتج فيه للقراءات المأثورة احتجاجا من جانب العربية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p40/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p40/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p40/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that when asked which Quranic knowledge is best, the Prophet answered its Arabic language and advised seeking it in poetry.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p40/r1.anchor: روى ابن عباس أن رجلا سأل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: أي علم القرآن أفضل؟ فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «عربيته فالتمسوها في الشعر»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p40/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p40/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p40/r2.claim: The Prophet urges careful parsing of the Quran and investigation of its rare vocabulary, saying God loves grammatical elucidation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p40/r2.anchor: وقال أيضا صلى الله عليه وسلم: «أعربوا القرآن والتمسوا غرائبه فإن الله يحب أن يعرب»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p40/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p40/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p40/r3.claim: Quranic grammar is foundational to the law because its legal meanings depend on it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p40/r3.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد عبد الحق رضي الله عنه: إعراب القرآن أصل في الشريعة، لأن بذلك تقوم معانيه التي هي الشرع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p40/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p40/r4.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p40/r4.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya interprets “wisdom” in the cited verse as understanding the Quran.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p40/r4.anchor: وقال أبو العالية في تفسير قوله عز وجل: ومن يؤت الحكمة فقد أوتي خيرا كثيرا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p40/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p40/r5.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p40/r5.claim: Qatāda interprets “wisdom” as the Quran and understanding its jurisprudence.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p40/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p40/r6.speaker: غيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p40/r6.claim: Another authority interprets “wisdom” as Quranic exegesis.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p40/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p40/r7.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p40/r7.claim: When challenged for calling Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh learned, ʿAlī explains that Jābir knew the interpretation of the cited verse about the return to God.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p40/r7.anchor: وذكر علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه جابر بن عبد الله فوصفه بالعلم، فقال له رجل: جعلت فداك، تصف جابرا بالعلم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p40/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p40/r8.speaker: الشعبي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p40/r8.claim: Al-Shaʿbī recounts that Masrūq traveled first to Basra and then to Syria to find the interpreter of a verse and learn its explanation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p40/r8.anchor: وقال الشعبي: رحل مسروق إلى البصرة في تفسير آية، فقيل له: إن الذي يفسرها رحل إلى الشام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p40/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p40/r9.speaker: إياس بن معاوية
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p40/r9.claim: Iyyās ibn Muʿāwiya compares readers without exegesis to people unable to read a king’s letter at night for lack of a lamp; a commentator supplies the light to understand it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p40/r9.anchor: وقال إياس بن معاوية: مثل الذين يقرؤون القرآن وهم لا يعلمون تفسيره كمثل قوم جاءهم كتاب من ملكهم ليلا وليس عندهم مصباح

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p40/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p40/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p40/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās likens someone who reads without explaining the Quran to a Bedouin who rapidly recites poetry without understanding it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p40/r10.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: «الذي يقرأ ولا يفسر كالأعرابي الذي يهذ الشعر»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p40/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p40/r11.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p40/r11.claim: Mujāhid says God most loves those who know best what He revealed.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p40/r11.anchor: وقال مجاهد: «أحب الخلق إلى الله أعلمهم بما أنزل»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p40/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p40/r12.speaker: الحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p40/r12.claim: Al-Ḥasan says he wishes every verse were understood in terms of its occasion and intended meaning.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p40/r12.anchor: وقال الحسن: «والله ما أنزل الله آية إلا أحب أن يعلم فيمن أنزلت وما يعني بها»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p40/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p40/r13.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p40/r13.claim: The Prophet says full understanding requires recognizing the Quran’s many possible aspects.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p40/r13.anchor: وقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «لا يفقه الرجل كل الفقه حتى يرى للقرآن وجوها كثيرة»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p40/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p40/r14.speaker: الحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p40/r14.claim: Al-Ḥasan blames weak Arabic command for readers getting stuck among a verse’s possible readings and then falsely speaking about God.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p40/r14.anchor: وقال الحسن: «أهلكتهم العجمة، يقرأ أحدهم الآية فيعيى بوجوهها حتى يفتري على الله فيها»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p40/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p40/r15.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p40/r15.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās began his teaching sessions with the Quran, then exegesis, then Hadith.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p40/r15.anchor: وكان ابن عباس يبدأ في مجلسه بالقرآن ثم بالتفسير ثم بالحديث

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p40/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p40/r16.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p40/r16.claim: ʿAlī says the Quran contains knowledge of everything, though an individual’s judgment may fail to grasp it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p40/r16.anchor: وقال علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه: «ما من شيء إلا وعلمه في القرآن ولكن رأي الرجل يعجز عنه»

JISHUMI:v1p191/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p191/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p191/r1.claim: Understanding the Qurʾān's meanings and rulings is the most important religious science because religion depends on it.
JISHUMI:v1p191/r1.anchor: ومن أجل العلوم معرفة كتاب الله تعالى، وتفهم معانيه وأحكامه، فإن عليه مدار الدين

JISHUMI:v1p191/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p191/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p191/r2.claim: The author says the Qurʾān was revealed, protected from alteration, addition, and omission, and made to supersede other religions.
JISHUMI:v1p191/r2.anchor: وأنزل القرآن، وصانه عن التحريف والزيادة والنقصان، ونسخ به سائر الأديان

JISHUMI:v1p191/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p191/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p191/r3.claim: Early scholars had precedence and laid foundations; later scholars improved arrangement, refinement, and benefits.
JISHUMI:v1p191/r3.anchor: وللأولين فضل السبق، وتأسيس الأمر، وللآخرين حسن الترتيب

JISHUMI:v1p191/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p191/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p191/r4.claim: He says this book gathers Qurʾānic sciences without tedious length or deficient brevity, to instruct beginners and remind advanced readers.
JISHUMI:v1p191/r4.anchor: وقد جمعت في كتابي هذا جما وجوامع في علم القرآن من غير تطويل ممل، أو إيجاز مخل

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p37/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p37/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p37/r1.claim: One area of Quran interpretation draws on Arabic, specifically vocabulary and grammatical inflection.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p37/r1.anchor: القسم الثاني : ما يرجع فيه إلى لسان العرب ، وذلك

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p37/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p37/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p37/r2.claim: Knowledge of vocabulary is required of the commentator but not the Quran reciter as such.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p37/r2.anchor: فأما اللغة ، فيكون العلم بها في حق المفسر دون القارئ

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p37/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p37/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p37/r3.claim: For vocabulary issues that do not entail action, a commentator may rely on one or two reports and cite one or two poetic lines.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p37/r3.anchor: جاز أن يعمل فيه على خبر الواحد والإثنين ، وأن يستشهد فيه من الشعر

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p37/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p37/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p37/r4.claim: If a vocabulary issue affects action, it requires widely transmitted evidence and mutually corroborating poetry, rather than one or two reports or verses.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p37/r4.anchor: لم يعمل فيه على خبر الواحد والإثنين ، ولا يستشهد فيه بالبيت والبيتين

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p37/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p37/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p37/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that when a man asked which Quranic knowledge is best, the Prophet answered its rare vocabulary and directed people to seek it in poetry; no grading is stated.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p37/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس : أن رجلا سأل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ، أي علم القرآن أفضل

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p37/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p37/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p37/r6.claim: Rare words are singled out because of their connection to the Quran's inimitability; poetry is the register of Arab speech and evidence for their meanings.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p37/r6.anchor: وإنما خص الغريب لاختصاصه بإعجاز القرآن ، وأحال عن الشعر لأنه ديوان كلامهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p37/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p37/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p37/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas advises seeking in poetry whatever is unclear in God's Book, since poetry is the register of the Arabs; no grading is stated.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p37/r7.anchor: وقد قال ابن عباس : ' إذا أشكل عليكم الشيء من كتاب الله ، فالتمسوه في الشعر

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p37/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p37/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p37/r8.claim: When a grammatical difference changes a ruling or interpretation, both commentator and reciter must know it: the commentator to determine the ruling and the reciter to avoid error.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p37/r8.anchor: فإن كان اختلافه موجبا لاختلاف حكمه وتغيير تأويله ، لزم العلم به في حق المفسر

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p37/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p37/r9.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p37/r9.claim: A saying attributed to the Prophet commands parsing the Quran and seeking its rare expressions; no grading is stated.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p37/r9.anchor: وروي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ، أنه قال : ' أعربوا القرآن والتمسوا غرائبه '

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p37/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p37/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p37/r10.claim: If inflection does not change the ruling or interpretation, it remains necessary for the reciter to avoid mistakes but is not required for a commentator who can identify the ruling without it; ignorance is still a general deficiency.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p37/r10.anchor: كان العلم بإعرابه لازما في حق القارئ ليسلم من اللحن في تأويلاته ، ولم يلزم في حق المفسر

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p37/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p37/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p37/r11.claim: A third area relies on scholarly reasoning: interpreting ambiguous text, deriving rulings, clarifying general wording, and specifying universal language.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p37/r11.anchor: ما يرجع فيه إلى اجتهاد العلماء ، وهو تأويل المتشابه ، واستنباط الأحكام

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p37/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p37/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p37/r12.claim: Legal scholars are best suited to this interpretation because they apply the principles of sacred law so that meanings do not conflict with them.
